processing: Ripe pu-erh blended to an average of grade 6 leaf from several Menghai growing areas, then pressed into cakes.
harvest_season: Not tied to one picking: it is a blend of already fermented material.
appearance_dry: A brown cake of mid-grade ripe leaf, as usual for a grade 6 Menghai blend.
appearance_liquor: Dark red-brown, as usual for Menghai ripe pu-erh.
appearance_wet: Soft, mid-sized dark brown leaf, as usual for a grade 6 blend.
taste_profile: Described as close in style to the 7562 recipe; expect the typical Menghai ripe profile of earth, wood and dark sweetness.

brewing.notes: Standard ripe handling: rinse once and use near-boiling water. A fresh pressing may benefit from some rest.

vintage_note: Sold by year and batch: the 2018 pressing, for example, carries batch 1801, the first batch of that year. Like other Dayi ripe cakes it can be drunk fairly young, and a recent pressing usually softens with a few years of storage.
description:
0562 is a Menghai Tea Factory ripe recipe often explained by reference to an older one. A retailer describes it as a blend introduced in 2005 in the style of the classic 7562, but drawing on tea from across Menghai's growing areas.

The leaf averages grade 6, so it sits in the middle of the factory's range: not bud-heavy like the small-leaf recipes and not stem-heavy like the coarse ones. The material is fermented first, then blended and pressed.

Expect a familiar Menghai ripe cup, with earth and wood and a dark sweetness. Close comparison notes with 7562 are scarce, so it is worth trying the two side by side if you can. Use very hot water and a quick rinse.

Buy by batch code, and treat the number as a house recipe that may shift a little between productions.
history: The Menghai Tea Factory became fully private in 1996 and adopted the Dayi mark. According to a retailer, 0562 appeared as a new blend in 2005, modelled on 7562. The factory has not published much on the recipe, and pressings such as the 2018 batch 1801 are the clearest record of it.
